title: Why Do We DREAM? 💭
description:
You slap your alarm clock... in an exam hall, in your pajamas. Relax: you're dreaming. Nobody knows for sure why we dream, but one leading idea is that the sleeping brain runs a kind of fire drill: it rehearses the things you fear while the part that checks logic is turned down, which is why nobody in the dream minds the pajamas. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

In one French study of 719 medical students, those who dreamed about their entrance exam the night before scored a little higher (8.5 against 7.8 out of 20). That is a link, not proof, and other ideas say dreams file memories or work through feelings. Meanwhile your brain switches off most of your muscles during dream sleep, so the drill stays in your head. Usually.
